criteria.criterion: The follow camera never places the camera beyond the solved clear distance for any input (the resolved parameter is always at most the clear distance reported by the collision query); when the clear distance is under the hard minimum in a sealed pocket, the avatar's own body is handled without entering geometry (for example by fading or hiding avatar meshes near the camera, or lifting toward the pivot), with the chosen approach documented in a code comment; a test with an always-immediate-hit query asserts the camera is not beyond the reported clear distance and fails on commit 3c888d6.
criteria.evidence: followCamera.ts pullIn: t = max(reach, floor) with the HARD_MIN push-out removed, so the resolved parameter never exceeds sol.t (reach <= sol.t and floor <= sol.t). Sealed-pocket body handling: the near plane is raised to (camera distance + 0.35 m) whenever the clear distance is under HARD_MIN (0.45), clipping the avatar's own meshes around the camera without moving the camera into the collider; restored to 0.1 otherwise and at beginEntry/beginExit; documented in a code comment. New tests: always-immediate-hit query asserts distance to anchor <= 0 with near >= 0.3 and a finite orientation; a sweep over clear distances 0..1.5 with varying look input asserts distance <= clear + 1e-6; near plane restore test. Run on 3c888d6 version of followCamera.ts: 3 tests failed (log: <scratchpad>/xfix/test-on-3c888d6.log); with the fix 105 passed in followCamera*.test.ts and the full suite 637 passed.

lessonsProposed: A repeated clamp such as Math.max(reach, floor, HARD_MIN/len) can silently override the collision-solved distance; assert the camera distance against the distance the collision query reported, not against a fixed minimum.
In zsh, env "$cfg" with a variable holding several VAR=val words does not word-split; use a bash script with explicit args, otherwise harness options are silently ignored.
